rationale:
I shot the town before planning it — a clear late-summer afternoon (day 8, 15.2 h, 75 people), a rainy early-summer night, a spring afternoon, wide and phone — and the first thing to report is a brief I did NOT write. c232 has ridden three manager passes on the claim that the near roof band is 13% of a desktop frame and 22% of a phone's and reads as one flat ashlar texture. The cue itself said: measure it as its own luma class first. So I measured it: sd/mean 0.281 over the tight band (x 500-2300, y 1370-1560 of a 3200x1900 wide shot, seed 42, day 8 15.2 h), against WALL 0.240, courtyard paving 0.212, WATER 0.177 and ROAD 0.150. It is the HIGHEST-variance large surface on the record, not the flattest. And drawNearRoof's own comment says the darkness is the point — 'bright town, slate mid-tone, then a foreground that falls away into the sill instead of competing with the courtyard for the eye' — over a band that already carries slates on their own lattice, per-slate moss and soot and slipped tiles, wells, dormers, a parapet with a lead gutter and hopper heads, awnings, 24 pieces of furniture a bay, roof birds and the cat's ridge. Cue closed on evidence. That is 90 minutes of worker time that would have been spent proving a premise wrong, which is the fault the WATCH item aims at me, and I would rather spend the measurement here than there.

The rung is 5 and the argument is the coverage grid read by KIND rather than by domain. In 164 iterations the town has had twelve Interaction entries, six of them in the Sill, and four domains — Lane, Cross street, River, Sky — have never had one. Meanwhile the observer's relationship with the town is complete in every direction except one: you can NAME anything under the pointer (beds, plots, paving, trees, people, birds, faces, vanes, the field edge), you can go to five fixed quarters, you can skip to the evening or the morning, pause, and change speed. What you cannot do is FOLLOW. The town holds 75 people on a summer afternoon, every one on an errand that ends in a stop that performs something and usually says it at one of 37 sayAt sites, and the camera has never once been pointed at something that moves. b166 is the bet: click a person and the frame takes them. It is rung 5 by the ladder's own words — a new way to READ the town — it lands in the thinnest cell in the grid, and it compounds the four best-built systems the run has (the quarter camera and its ease, the pointer naming, the three-rank ticker, and the visit). 90 minutes, 150-300 lines stated as expected and welcome, and both failure modes priced into `avoid`: the ground cache (drawGround is 25-27 ms, c214, and a camera that moves every frame must hold the padded wide cache the way whereGo's ease already does rather than rebuild) and the world's edge clamps.

b165 goes FIRST and it is deliberately the bet's runway. c250 said backKey has no camera term; I read it on HEAD and it is exactly so — courtyard.html:6513 keys the cached backdrop on `W + 'x' + H + ':' + lightBucket` while the line above it computes `hz = topPad - 3.4 * cellH` live, and stepView moves both topPad and s every frame of a 0.9 s ease and leaves them moved at a quarter, where s reaches 3.6. So the live gradient's horizon and the cached hills part company during every camera move the town already has, and b166 is about to put a camera in front of it that moves continuously. Fix the runway before you drive on it. The other two take the next two longest-untouched domains on cues that have aged enough to be briefs: b168 is c245, the four lawn kinds #157 left with an unpriced walk home, and b169 is c249 with the spent lapse-hours WATCH item folded into it — #161 disproved the empty-morning premise on 125 counted mornings, so the morning's fault is composition (11.6 errand kinds against the evening's 14.2), not headcount, and the brief carries that number and its probe by name.

b167 is the firing signal and I have done the diagnosis rather than passing the symptom along. The quota gate #149 built and #153 wired has measured nothing on any of the twelve rows that carry the field. The code is right — running it by hand exits 0 with a full report. The runner is one bash process that has been alive since Wed 02:00, started before #153 landed, and bash reads a script by byte offset, so a live loop executes the text it was launched with. The signal's own advice, 'restart the runner', is correct and is a human's move; the loop's move is to stop depending on the shell for the reading, so b167 has runlog.mjs compute the quota itself when the runner did not hand it one. That is #164's own law applied to the thing that produced it: a field is not a reading. It carries c252 with it (build-stats.mjs greps quota zero times, so a breach is invisible in stats.html, my other input) and the closedCues pruner, which is 79 KB of the 114 KB state.json.

CURATION. Coverage was five iterations stale — #160-#164 had never been recorded and lastIteration was stuck at 159, so the grid I rotate from could not see a fifth of the run since my predecessor's pass. LAWS.md: five claims promoted out of #160-#164 and every one MERGED into the law that owns the subject, never stacked — #161's dated-scarcity into locate-before-you-judge (which already carries 'count it on HEAD'), #160's instrument-the-PAYOFF into the rate-of-zero law, #162's a-cached-layer-drawn-over-a-live-one-SUBTRACTS into the legibility law, #163's offscreen-context-is-not-accelerated into the CACHE/COMPOSITE law, #164's a-field-is-not-a-reading into the probe law. The file was 23 bytes from its cap, so all five were paid for by CUTS, and these are the named ones: the small-n quantile clause in the seeded-world law (subsumed by the gathering law's SHARE-over-a-long-run / COIN-over-a-short-one, which is its general form); the open-it-a-trip-earlier and hour-the-last-person-is-GONE clauses (bound BOTH ends survives and carries them); the season-scaling explanation and the whole social-window-INTERSECT sentence in the sun's-hour law (#148 landed it and it is a special case of two rules already there); the why-the-sweep-reveals-it clause in the cap-versus-share law; the frame-cost.mjs/perf.mjs parenthetical (the probe law says it better and at length); the 5.4-cell-wall example in renderer trap (f); the where-inView-has-already-filtered clause in the FRAMING law; the census-churns-everywhere restatement; the drawn-live-or-painted-INTO-the-cache aside; and the frames-drawn-at-page-load explanation in the probe law. 12 laws, 12,276 / 12,288 B, five more claims than it started with. Cues 11 -> 7: four promoted into this queue (c245, c249, c250, c252), one CLOSED on measurement (c232, above), one raised (c253, the manager's own uncapped read surface). Watch 5 -> 4: the lapse-hours item is spent into b169 and its standing rule — supply for either hour is its own source, never a laneCap share — goes into the brief where it can bind; the measure-a-surface item now carries the near-roof number; and a new item warns the next pass that a camera which moves every frame is a different animal from whereGo's ease. Worker budget 45.3 -> 45.0 / 46 KB, every sub-cap met.

One thing I am NOT doing and want on the record, for the second pass running: seven of the twelve laws are over rotate-ledger's 900 B per-law advisory. The file is twelve fat compound laws rather than sixty thin ones. My predecessor said a future pass should SPLIT before it appends; I appended, because splitting saves no bytes against the binding cap and the compound laws' connective tissue is doing real work — 'a walk is priced at its CHOICE and spent on its way' only means anything with the four sentences after it. But that is now two passes of the same deferral, and a third would be the pattern this seat exists to catch.

So the live sky gradient's horizon slides and the cached hills, ranks and skyline stay exactly where they were painted: they part company during every camera move the town already has, and at a quarter the backdrop is drawn at 1x behind a town at 2-3x. The answer is next door: drawGround paints ONE padded wide cache and the blit scales it by `k = viewS/gview.s` with an origin offset (courtyard.html:10137-10138). Wide (whereN 0) must come out bit-identical, or the census and the motion gate churn on kinds you never touched. No new R() draw.

queue.brief: THE BET — take the swing; a 150-300 line diff is expected and welcome. The town holds 75 people on a summer afternoon, every one of them on an errand that ends in a stop that performs something and usually says it (sayAt, 37 sites). The observer can NAME any of them under the pointer and can go to five fixed quarters — and the camera has never once been pointed at something that moves. Click a person and the frame takes them: it eases onto them at a readable zoom, keeps them in the picture as they walk, tells you in the ticker who they are and what they are doing, and lets go — easing back where you came from — when their errand ends, when they leave the world, or when you click away. A visitor who clicks once learns in ten seconds that this is a town of individuals with somewhere to be, which no amount of staring at the wide shot will teach them. A quarter is DATA (QUARTERS is a list of boxes with air/keep/share that viewFor fits), so the cheapest honest shape for a follow is a box that MOVES with its subject and leaves viewFor, inView and the ease working unchanged.
queue.successLooksLike: On a desktop at Wide, clicking a walker eases the frame onto them; they stay in the picture for the whole of their errand while the town carries on around them; the ticker names them and their stop as it happens; the follow releases cleanly on any of the three exits and eases back. frame-cost.mjs shows no new per-frame ground rebuild, and the ordinary Wide frame is unchanged when nothing is being followed.
queue.avoid: THE GROUND CACHE IS THE WHOLE RISK, and whereGo has already solved it once: an ease survives only because it paints the padded WIDE cache once (groundPad/gpadWant/gview), scales the blit by `k = viewS/gview.s`, and repaints the destination ONCE on arrival. drawGround costs 25-27 ms (c214), so a follow that sets groundDirty per frame drops every frame. Hold the padded wide cache for the whole follow and repaint once on release. FACES are registered in gview's frame and faceAt maps through the same k — keep that true. Do not exceed VIEW_SMAX or drop held()'s WORLD_X0/WORLD_X1 clamps, or the frame runs off the world into the cache's column repeat. Agents are transient: one whose route ends off the world must release the follow, never snap. Wide must stay exempt in inView and bit-identical while nothing is followed — the census and motion gates depend on it. No new R() draw: a click is not a seeded event. And do NOT fix the backdrop's stale horizon in here; that is b165's.

queue.brief: The morning is not empty — #161 proved that and rejected the brief that said otherwise. probes/lapse-pop.mjs counted 125 mornings (5 seeds x a year) at mean 28.3 people, min 6, against the evening's 41.1. The gap is COMPOSITION: 11.6 errand KINDS at sunUp+0.5 against 14.2 at sunDown+1, and the evening's extra kinds are ones the morning has no analogue of — the dusk crowd, the tap, the band, the homers. The morning has the sweeper, the round and the cart, and those are 2.4 of its 28.3 people. Give the morning two kinds of its own and build them properly rather than four thinly: the town's own nouns suggest shutters and awnings going up on the kiosk and the cafe before the tables are set, a delivery at the tap's door (TAP_DOOR and callIn exist, and rutF's own comment records that the tap's drinkers never set foot on the road), the allotment gate being opened, the glasshouse being aired. Each on its OWN source and its own clock. Re-run the probe on HEAD first and quote it.
